definitions.explanation: So wrong, offensive, or harmful that it cannot be forgiven or overlooked.

examples.japanese: {許|ゆる}し{難|がた}い{行為|こうい}だ。
{仲間|なかま}を{裏切|うらぎ}るとは{許|ゆる}し{難|がた}い。
{弱|よわ}い{立場|たちば}の{人|ひと}をだまして{金|かね}を{奪|うば}うのは{許|ゆる}し{難|がた}い{罪|つみ}だ。
examples.english: Deceiving people in a vulnerable position to take their money is an inexcusable crime.

notes:
Formed from {許|ゆる}す (to forgive) + the suffix ～{難|がた}い (hard to ~). It expresses strong moral condemnation and has a formal, somewhat literary tone.

USAGE:
The ～{難|がた}い pattern attaches to verb stems to mean "difficult to ~": {理解|りかい}し{難|がた}い (hard to understand), {信|しん}じ{難|がた}い (hard to believe). {許|ゆる}し{難|がた}い is stronger and more formal than {許|ゆる}せない.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {許|ゆる}し{難|がた}い{行為|こうい}: an unforgivable act
- {許|ゆる}し{難|がた}い{罪|つみ}: an inexcusable crime

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {許|ゆる}せない: unforgivable — more colloquial and emotional
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い: unbearable; hard to endure
